episodes.157616: Similar to the previous day, and shifted further toward the southeast, an approaching cold front combined with warm moist air and an unstable atmosphere to develop and sustain severe thunderstorms through some eastern Montana locations during the evening hours.
episodes.157772: A severe thunderstorm produced hail up to quarter size near Castle Rock, along with locally heavy rain and minor street flooding.
episodes.157796: Scattered to numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms developed throughout the day on June 5th, ahead of a stationary cut off upper low pressure system over Central Texas. Daytime heating contributed to moderate instability within a very moist air mass in place.  These showers and thunderstorms were very efficient rainfall producers as they moved slowly and often trained over the same areas over a given period of time. Showers and thunderstorms containing heavy rainfall developed over much of Panola County during the late afternoon through the evening, with widespread rainfall amounts of 4-8 inches falling over this area. These amounts fell over already saturated grounds from heavy rainfall which fell a day prior, with two day totals of 6-12 inches observed. This resulted in widespread flash flooding across Southern and Eastern Panola County, where multiple roads were covered in high rushing water, including Highway 59 just south of Carthage. These showers and isolated thunderstorms finally diminished during the late evening hours.
episodes.157851: A couple of isolated thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts across portions of southeast Montana.
episodes.158007: Severe thunderstorms occurred along a cold front that pushed into western and central North Dakota where strong instability and enhanced deep layer shear were noted. Strong wind gusts became the main threat, though one storm did produce large hail in Stark County. The strongest reported wind gusts, estimated at 70 mph, occurred at Beulah in Mercer County.
episodes.158264: Severe thunderstorm outflow winds were measured across portions of eastern Carbon and Platte Counties with wind speeds in excess of 58 mph.
episodes.159146: Heavy rain in early June brought flooding to several rivers in central and northeast Arkansas.
episodes.159267: As an upper-level low pressure system moved over central parts of the country, a few storm systems moved across the state of Mississippi. These brought rounds of severe thunderstorms and heavy rain to the region, eventually leading to the first wave of significant flooding in Mississippi this month. Over 200 homes were flooded in portions of Bolivar and Sunflower Counties.
episodes.159506: A broad low pressure center in the middle and upper atmosphere moved from northern Texas to northeastern Oklahoma on the 6th and 7th. The first round of thunderstorms affected southeastern Oklahoma during the morning and afternoon hours of the 6th. Locally heavy rainfall occurred, which resulted in isolated flash flooding. ||A more pronounced and focused area of thunderstorms developed during the early morning hours of the 7th across northeastern Oklahoma. The storms were slow-moving, and very efficient rain producers due to high amounts of moisture in the air. A swath of heavy rain occurred across portions of McIntosh, Okfuskee, Okmulgee, Tulsa, and Pawnee Counties, where widespread two to eight inch amounts occurred. Personal weather stations in Okmulgee County measured over thirteen inches of rain in a several hour period, with rainfall rates as much as six and a half inches per hour. Widespread flash flooding occurred as a result of this heavy rainfall.
episodes.159644: Numerous thunderstorms developed during the late evening of the 6th into the early morning of the 7th as a low level jet strengthened across southwestern Oklahoma and western north Texas. Reports of strong wind gusts, hail, and isolated flooding were received.
episodes.159661: Thunderstorms developed along a stalled frontal boundary during the afternoon of the 6th. An isolated severe thunderstorm produced damaging wind gusts in the town of Lagrange.
episodes.160001: An upper level low centered over Texas aided in the transfer of deeper Gulf moisture to the region. Precipitable moisture values were well above climatological average. This increased moisture combined with increasing instability in the afternoon created an environment able to sustain a severe thunderstorm over the coastal waters. This storm produced winds in excess of gale force.
episodes.160075: Thunderstorm development on this day was mainly confined to the I-25 Corridor and westward, with burn scar flash flooding a primary concern on this day. While this was the main concern, an isolated severe storm did occur across the eastern plains, as well as a brief landspout tornado occurring over the San Luis Valley. This tornado was brief, and did not produce any damage.
episodes.160095: A severe thunderstorm developed near Victoria during the afternoon of the 5th. The storm produced wind damage on the southwest side of Victoria.
episodes.160096: Heavy rain produced street flooding in North Myrtle Beach.
episodes.160111: Scattered thunderstorms developed across western North Carolina during the afternoon and evening. Slow movement of the storms resulted in localized very heavy rainfall, causing flash flooding to develop in south Charlotte. At least one of the storms also produced hail.
episodes.160218: Strong thunderstorm developed in southeast Mississippi and produced locally heavy rain along with strong wind gusts that caused some damage.
episodes.160279: Thunderstorm clusters formed during the evening hours of June 5th, with several storms producing damaging wind gusts. This episode went through the early morning hours on June 6th. Hail up to one inch was reported.
episodes.160281: Thunderstorm clusters formed during the evening hours of June 5th, with several storms producing damaging wind gusts. This episode went through the early morning hours on June 6th. Hail up to one inch was reported.
episodes.160374: A series of mesoscale convective complexes developed over western portions of the Southern Plains and dived southeast through North and Central Texas, producing isolated instances of flooding and wind damage. On June 6th, a female died in her vehicle while crossing a flooded creek in Garland.
